themes.theme_description: Appreciate and be able to apply science in the management and conservation of the environment

topics.core_competency: The learner appreciates the importance of science in the management and conservation of the environment.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand the meaning of air pollution (u)
identify the major air pollutants and their sources (k)
assess the different ways of preventing air pollution (u, v/a)
understand the meaning of water pollution and identify the main water pollutants (k, u)
analyse the effects of water pollution and suggest the ways of preventing water pollution (u)
understand the term solid waste material and identify different types of solid waste (k, u)
appreciate the dangers of solid waste and suggests ways of managing solid waste (u, v/a)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups or as individuals, learners use ICT or other sources to research and hold interactive discussions on the various ways of preventing air pollution. Make a presentation at the end of the discussion.
research and make presentations on water pollutants, effects of polluted water and ways of preventing water pollution
design a project to collect, prevent and minimize solid waste materials at or around the school.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Many homesteads in Africa use firewood for cooking in small non-ventilated kitchens. Basing on the above statement and in a conversation, task learners to answer the following questions: State the dangers associated with this practice; How can cooking in such kitchens be made safer

project_requirements.project_scope_verbatim: design a project to collect, prevent and minimize solid waste materials at or around the school.
project_requirements.deliverables_verbatim: Project design and execution at or around the school

suggested_uses: use ICT or other sources to research

topics.core_competency: The learner understands how climate changes affect life and how they can be mitigated.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: compare weather and climate (u)
know the various weather measuring equipment and discuss how each one is used (k, u)
demonstrate how to measure using weather measuring equipment (u, s)
analyse how man’s activities can lead to climate change (u, v/a)
assess the effects climate changes on life and the environment (agriculture, settlement, vegetation, water cycle, etc.) (u, s)
prepare a weather chart (u, s)
relate climate to vegetation zones (u)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, and with guidance from the teacher, learners; identify the elements of climate, and discuss how each element affects agriculture
visit a Meteorological Station, observe various weather measuring equipment and satellite images and how they are used
practise the use of some of the meteorology equipment and collect data by using the equipment and make a simple weather chart
relate the weather charts to activities undertaken by humans in the locality
identify agencies involved in providing weather and climatic information to the public and discuss their roles

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Suggest reasons why certain crops grow in some parts of the country while they may not thrive in others. Assess how learners communicate scientifically and efficiently.

practicals.title: Use of meteorology equipment
practicals.description_verbatim: practise the use of some of the meteorology equipment and collect data by using the equipment and make a simple weather chart

topic_metadata.topic_title: CONSERVATION AND SUSTAINABLE USE OF THE ENVIRONMENT

topics.core_competency: The learner appreciates the need to conserve the environment for future generations.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand the meaning of sustainable resource (u)
know the renewable and non-renewable resources in Uganda (k)
understand the importance of forests and water bodies in ecosystem balance (u)
understand the need to conserve fossil fuels (u)
analyse how wildlife, forest and fish resources can be maintained (u)
appreciate the need for conservation programmes and the roles of communities in conservation (u, v/a)

must_cover: importance of forests and water bodies
maintenance of wildlife, forest and fish resources

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups and with guidance from the teacher, learners; discuss conservation activities that can be carried out at school and explain the impact of the activities on a global scale
debate the motion “High population growth is the principle cause of global environmental problems”

suggested_assessment_activities.description: A school conservation club makes briquettes from waste paper. In a conversation, task learners to explain how using briquettes in place of charcoal helps to promote conservation.
Task learners, in a conversation to name four endangered species in Africa, give reasons that caused them to be endangered and state what is being done to protect them.

themes.theme_description: Appreciate and be able to apply science in industrial processes and effective utilisation of resources.

topics.core_competency: The learner understands how industrial processes produce useful materials which contribute greatly to the economic growth of Uganda as a nation.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: know the common industrial materials in our homes and identify their uses (k, u)
identify factors that favour the establishment of particular industries (u)
understand the contribution of the industries to society (u)
assess the problems arising from industrial development (u, v/a)
know ores from which iron, copper, sodium and aluminium are extracted (k)
understand steps involved in the extraction of copper, iron and sodium (details of chemical reactions not required) (k, u)
know the major mining centres in Uganda (k)
understand the factors that favour the establishment of a metal plant (u)
identify the uses of: iron, copper and aluminium and explain why each is used in these ways (u)
identify the raw materials for industrial manufacture of ammonia and explains how these materials are obtained (u)
understand the commercial manufacture of ammonia (u)
understand the importance ammonia in fertilizer industry (u)
appreciate the potential dangers to the environment of excessive use of fertilizers (u)
know the other sources of industrial fertilizers used to improve crop growth (k)
understand the process of the manufacture cement (u)
know the changes that take place during the setting of cement (k)
know what acidic rain is and how it affects concrete materials (k, u)
know the meaning of petroleum and its importance in industrial processes (k)
understand how petroleum products are used and misused and the consequences resulting from the misuse (u)
understand the meaning of fermentation and explain its industrial application in the production of ethanol/alcoholic beverages (k, u)
understand the manufacture of an alcoholic drink in their community (u, s)
appreciate the use and misuse of alcoholic drinks ( u, v/a)
know what soaps and detergents are (u)
understand the industrial process used in the manufacture of soaps and detergents (u)
understand how soaps remove dirt from clothes (u)
appreciate dangers associated with use of soaps and detergents (u, v/a)

must_cover: ores of iron, copper, sodium, aluminium
extraction steps of copper, iron, sodium

explicitly_excluded.text_verbatim: details of chemical reactions not required

depth_limitations.text_verbatim: details of chemical reactions not required

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups or as individuals, learners; research about the reasons that favour the establishment of some of the industries where they are located
discuss the main sources of environmental damage in Uganda that are caused by utilising natural resources

In groups or as individuals, learners research and discuss: the common industrial processes for extracting the metals from the ores and classify each process as a chemical or physical change; how copper and iron are purified from the crude products of smelting; how used metals are recycled and why it is important

In groups or as individuals, learners: discuss the importance of nitrate fertilisers for growing food; discuss how eutrophication results from excessive fertiliser use and how it damages our environment; discuss the importance of other fertilizers (non-nitrogenous) and their importance; discuss the effects of overusing commercial fertilizers

In groups, learners; discuss the manufacture of cement from limestone and its environmental impact; discuss how concrete is made from cement and explain why it is often sprayed with water while it is setting
carry out an experiment to demonstrate the action of acids on cement
use ICT and other sources to search and make a presentation on the petroleum products
carry out a discussion to identify some common plastic materials in our homes and their uses
carry out a discussion on the dangers of misuse of petroleum products (e.g. Burning, cooking in plastic /“kavera”, poor disposal, oil spills etc.)

In groups, learners discuss: The process of fermentation and identify the instances in everyday life where it occurs; the raw materials that can be used in the manufacture of ethanol and alcoholic beverages and discuss how the alcoholic beverages are manufactured
In groups or as individuals, learners: discuss how soap and detergents are manufactured from identified raw materials
prepare liquid soap in the home or at school and make a report
carry out a survey on local materials in their area that can be used as alternative raw materials for domestic soap production soap.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Describe some of the dangers to the community arising from these industrial processes.
Assess how learners communicate and develop values in relation to development
Locate the geographical place where copper, cobalt and iron metal ores are obtained in Uganda.
In a conversation, task learners to suggest the likely challenges which communities living around mining centres face.
engage learners in a debate to explain the effect of excessive use of fertilisers on our environment.
In a conversation, ask learners to name the materials that must be added to cement to make concrete. Ask learners why each of the materials is added to the cement.
Describe the dangers of the following: Boiling food covered in polythene material; Spilling fuel in your surrounding; Burning polythene; Poor disposal of plastics
Explain the social and scientific implications of alcohol. Assess how learners express themselves and how they communicate values and attitudes.
Explain the differences and similarities between soap and detergents in terms of composition, use and disposal challenges.

practicals.title: Action of acids on cement
practicals.description_verbatim: carry out an experiment to demonstrate the action of acids on cement

practicals.title: Preparation of liquid soap
practicals.description_verbatim: prepare liquid soap in the home or at school and make a report

suggested_uses: use ICT and other sources to search and make a presentation on the petroleum products

syllabus_notes.text_verbatim: details of chemical reactions not required

themes.theme_description: Appreciate the importance of science in conservation of and effective utilisation of energy.

topics.core_competency: The learner investigates the properties of transverse and longitudinal wave forms and appreciates that waves transmit energy.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand the meaning of a wave and classifies waves as mechanical and electromagnetic waves, transverse and longitudinal waves, progressive and stationary waves
know how waves transfer energy and the basic features of waves i.e. amplitude, wavelength, frequency, and period, velocity (k, u)
relate frequency and period of a wave (u, s)
use the wave equation: v = λ f to solve simple numerical problems (u, s)
understand how sound is produced and transmitted in terms of particle theory (u)
demonstrate that sound does not travel in vacuum (u, s)
understand why sound travels at different speeds in different states of matter (u)
know the difference between loudness, pitch and noise and discusses the factors which affect them (k, u)
demonstrate other properties of sound waves in terms of reflection and refraction, and compare them to those of light (u, s)
understand the terms echo and reverberation (u)
plan and carry out an activity to measure the velocity of sound in air using the echo method and comment on the result (u, s)
solve simple numerical problems related to echoes (u, s)
know the factors that affect the velocity of sound in air (k)
appreciate the applications of reflected sound waves (u, v/a)

must_cover: wave features (amplitude, wavelength, frequency, period, velocity)
speed of sound in different states
measurement of velocity of sound in air

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups or as individuals; learners demonstrate what waves are using ropes or water in a basin or pond
carry out an activity to demonstrate the movement of transverse and longitudinal waves
solve a numerical problem of this nature: In a progressive water wave, the distance between ten successive crests is 18 cm. If the frequency of the waves is 40 Hz, calculate the velocity of the waves
In groups and with guidance from the teacher, learners; carry out activity to produce sound and discuss what happens during the process
demonstrate that sound requires a medium to travel
carry out a discussion to compare sound and light waves and make a report
In groups, learners: plan and carry out an activity to measure the velocity of sound in air using the echo method and discuss the limitations of the method
in groups, learners work out this problem: A student standing 100 m from a large building blows a whistle and hears the echo after 0.6 s. Calculate the speed of sound in air

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Solve the problem: In a ripple tank, the distance between 10 successive crests is 18 cm and the frequency of the ripples is 50 Hz. Find the speed of the ripples.
Observe how learners state the formula and use it in the calculation, the substitution and how they express the final answer.
Compare sound and light waves in a group discussion and assess how learners express themselves and how they communicate
Solve the problem: A student standing 100 m from a large building blows a whistle and hears the echo after 0.6 s. Calculate the speed of sound in air.

practicals.title: Demonstration of waves
practicals.description_verbatim: learners demonstrate what waves are using ropes or water in a basin or pond

practicals.title: Movement of transverse and longitudinal waves
practicals.description_verbatim: carry out an activity to demonstrate the movement of transverse and longitudinal waves

practicals.title: Sound production
practicals.description_verbatim: carry out activity to produce sound and discuss what happens during the process

practicals.title: Sound transmission medium
practicals.description_verbatim: demonstrate that sound requires a medium to travel

practicals.title: Velocity of sound in air
practicals.description_verbatim: plan and carry out an activity to measure the velocity of sound in air using the echo method

themes.theme_description: Appreciate and be able to apply science to the development of technology to the development of mankind

topics.core_competency: The learner knows the properties of magnets and appreciates that the earth is a magnet itself.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: categorise materials as magnetic and non-magnetic, using simple tests (k, u)
demonstrate the test for magnets (u, s)
understand the meaning of ferromagnetic and para-magnetic materials, and state their applications (u, s)
demonstrate how like and unlike poles behave when brought together and use it to state the law of magnetism (u, s, gs)
know the general applications of magnets (k)
Demonstrate how to magnetise a magnetic material using stroking and induction, basing on the domain theory of magnets (u, s, gs)
Compare soft and hard magnetic materials and identify their applications (u, s)
Understand the different methods of demagnetisation and explain how demagnetisation occurs (u)

suggested_learning_activities.description: As individuals of in groups, learners: carry out activities to classify the following materials into magnetic or non- magnetic: copper, nickel, iron, steel, cobalt, aluminium, steel, zinc, wood, rubber
move magnets towards and away from other magnets and use the observations made to state the law of magnetism
As individuals or in groups, learners; carry out an activity to magnetise a steel nail/bar using single touch and test for its polarity
hold a chain of small nails or pins attached at the end of one pole of a permanent magnet and discuss the concept of induction using the observation

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Test for the presence of magnets. Assess how learners arrange their apparatus and how they state/write the observations
Draw diagrams to show the magnetic domains of a magnetised and un-magnetised metal bar and use this to explain the process of magnetisation and magnetic saturation.

practicals.title: Classification of magnetic materials
practicals.description_verbatim: carry out activities to classify the following materials into magnetic or non- magnetic: copper, nickel, iron, steel, cobalt, aluminium, steel, zinc, wood, rubber

practicals.title: Law of magnetism
practicals.description_verbatim: move magnets towards and away from other magnets and use the observations made to state the law of magnetism

practicals.title: Magnetisation by stroking
practicals.description_verbatim: carry out an activity to magnetise a steel nail/bar using single touch and test for its polarity

practicals.title: Magnetic induction
practicals.description_verbatim: hold a chain of small nails or pins attached at the end of one pole of a permanent magnet and discuss the concept of induction using the observation

topics.core_competency: The learner appreciates how electric current is generated and the limitations associated with the methods of generating electricity.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: know the meaning electric cell and emf and outline sources of emf (k, u)
know how emf is measured and state it’s units (u)
construct a simple cell and describes how it works (u, s)
know the limitations and suggests improvements to a simple cell (u, v/a)
compare between primary and secondary cells (u)
understand the structure and action of dry cells and accumulators (u, s)
understand the process of charging an accumulator and discuss its proper handling methods (u)
appreciate that there are different sources of electricity, citing particular examples in Uganda (u, v/a)
understand what electric current is, how it is measured, it’s units, what causes it and its effects (u)
understand the meaning of electric circuit and identify its components and types (k, u)
categorise materials as conductors, semiconductors and insulators and identify their applications (u)
compare a.c. and d.c. and explain what inverters and rectifiers are used for using examples of their use at home (k, u)
identify common domestic electrical appliances and establishes whether they operate on d.c. or a.c. (k, u)
know the importance of the components of domestic wiring (u, v/a)
appreciate the methods of saving electricity (u, v/a)

suggested_learning_activities.description: As individuals or in groups, learners: construct a simple cell from locally available materials and discuss why the emf of a cell gradually reduces
discuss the advantages and disadvantages of the various sources of electricity in Uganda
In groups, learners; discuss uses of conductors and insulators in reference to the domestic appliances
explain the importance of sockets, switches and circuit breakers in domestic wiring
categorise the common domestic appliances and classify them according to whether they operate on a.c or d.c

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe groups of learners construct a simple cell. Converse with learners about the materials used and the process of operation. Then assess the physical cell and the write up of its operation.

Task learners, in a class discussion to analyse the advantages and disadvantages of the various sources of electricity, with reference to Uganda. Assess the self-confidence, and the way learners communicate scientifically.
In a group, learners discuss the applications of insulators and semiconductors. In a conversation, ask learners to identify a variety of appliances in which semiconductors are applied.
Task learners to write an article advising communities about electric energy saving in the home. Assess how learners communicate scientifically and how they develop values.

practicals.title: Construction of a simple cell
practicals.description_verbatim: construct a simple cell from locally available materials

themes.theme_description: Appreciate that the body is made up of different systems working together to sustain life

topics.core_competency: The learner understands the various physiological changes during growth; the emotional and psychological challenges associated with each stage.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: know the difference between growth and development (k)
understand the importance of mitosis (u)
know the various stages of development in human life (physical and cognitive) (u, s)
relate the developmental stages of a child to significant features of behaviour at each stage (u, s)
understand the deviant behaviour that may be associated with the various physiological changes (u)
appreciate the physical, physiological, psychological (emotional) changes associated with adolescence and puberty and highlights the associated myths (u, v/a)
appreciate various features related to the process of aging (u, v/a)

must_cover: adolescence and puberty changes and myths

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners discuss: the physical and physiological changes that occur in humans during puberty; myths associated with sex, ejaculation, menstruation and pregnancy among adolescents; best practices of looking after the elderly

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Task learners to write down the challenges that teenagers face due to the body changes they undergo.
In a class discussion, ask learners to state the advice they would give to a student who is struggling with the changes taking place in him or her during puberty.

topics.core_competency: The learner understands between evolution, inheritance and variation and applies them correctly in scientific enquiries.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: know the traits that are inherited and those that are not inherited (k)
understand the meaning of variation, its types and causes (k, u)
understand the meaning of the term monohybrid inheritance (u)
know the terms used in monohybrid inheritance (Gene, chromosome, allele, homozygous, heterozygous) (k, u)
understand sex determination in humans (u)
appreciate how natural selection leads to evolution (k, u, v/a)

explicitly_excluded.text_verbatim: Doing crosses and Punett squares NOT required

depth_limitations.text_verbatim: Doing crosses and Punett squares NOT required

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups and with guidance from the teacher, learners: brainstorm on types and causes of variation stating examples
research, discuss and explain sex determination in humans

suggested_assessment_activities.description: In a class discussion, task learners to state the areas of everyday life where they think the knowledge of genetics is applicable.
